title: Dataclasses, enums, abstract base classes, and protocols
sources: Python 3.14 Standard Library: dataclasses, enum, abc, and typing.Protocol; reviewed 2026-10-03
masterChecklist: dataclass, enums, abstract base classes, protocols, design trade-offs
whyItMatters: As an application grows, plain dictionaries make valid states unclear. These tools let code name its data and capabilities without forcing unrelated objects into a rigid inheritance tree.
simpleExplanation: A dataclass generates routine data-container methods from annotated fields, but annotations are not automatic runtime validators. An enum names allowed states; a model field annotated with that enum still needs validation if callers could pass raw text. An abstract base class can require implemented methods before a subclass is instantiated. A protocol describes a required capability for static type checking without forcing common ancestry; it does not automatically check input at runtime.
mentalModel: A dataclass is a labelled form, an enum is a controlled dropdown, an abstract base class is an inherited job requirement, and a protocol is a capability checklist used by a type checker. Someone still has to validate submitted form values.
outcomes: Use Enum for a finite business state and validate external input.
Explain when an ABC provides runtime abstract-method enforcement.
Choose a protocol when capability matters more than ancestry.

realWorldExample.scenario: A learning service records a submission status and sends notifications through different channels.
realWorldExample.riskWithoutSetup: Free-form strings accept typos such as 'submited'; a plain dataclass annotation alone does not reject a raw status string, and integrations may be forced into an unnatural class hierarchy.
realWorldExample.professionalApproach: Convert external text to an enum member, validate the record in __post_init__, and use a focused notification protocol with an injected provider.

explanation: The dataclass generates an initializer and readable representation from annotated fields, but __post_init__ enforces the runtime Status contract.
Status('submitted') converts validated external text to a named member; unknown text raises ValueError.
Notifier is a structural type-checking contract. A plain annotation does not inspect objects at runtime.
workedExample.safeExperiment: Try Status('submited') and catch its ValueError. Compare enum members with Status.SUBMITTED, not a raw string.

procedure: Identify related data that belongs in one record.
Use a dataclass for simple record boilerplate, then validate business rules in __post_init__ or at a boundary.
Use Enum for a finite vocabulary and convert external text explicitly.
Use an ABC when an inherited runtime abstract-method guard is useful; prefer a focused Protocol for a structural capability.
Test direct invalid construction, not just the happy path.

commonMistakes.mistake: Treating dataclass annotations as runtime type enforcement.
commonMistakes.why: The generated initializer normally stores values without type checks.
commonMistakes.avoid: Validate in __post_init__ and convert external input first.

commonMistakes.mistake: Comparing an enum member to its plain string value.
commonMistakes.avoid: Compare members; use .value only at a text boundary.

commonMistakes.mistake: Creating deep inheritance for one required method.
commonMistakes.why: It couples unrelated providers and complicates substitution.
commonMistakes.avoid: Use a focused protocol and composition if a capability is all that is required.

lab.title: Model project states safely
lab.safety: The lab uses only local classes and fictional task data.
guidedSteps: In __post_init__, reject stage values that are not Stage members.
Make is_complete compare task.stage to Stage.DONE.
Create a TODO task and a DONE task using the enum member.
Attempt direct construction with the raw string 'done' and catch TypeError.
Try converting an unknown external string with Stage(...).
checks: A new task is TODO and reports False.
A raw string stage is rejected by the model.
An unknown external string is rejected by Enum conversion.
hints: Use Stage(text) when reading external data.
lab.solutionExplanation: The model's post-init check rejects a direct raw string, while enum-member comparisons make the status check explicit. External text should be converted using Stage(text) before construction.
challenges: Write a __post_init__ rule rejecting blank titles.

projectConnection.milestone: Replace free-form progress strings with a validated Stage enum and a Task dataclass.
projectConnection.definitionOfDone: Tests cover each stage, invalid direct construction, and conversion of external text before it becomes a Stage.

assessment.question: What does @dataclass commonly generate?
assessment.answer: An initializer and useful representation/equality behavior from fields.
assessment.explanation: It reduces routine record boilerplate but does not enforce every annotated type.

assessment.question: Why use Enum for status?
assessment.answer: It names a finite set of intended states, provided inputs are converted or validated.
assessment.explanation: An enum-annotated field can still hold a raw string if code does not check it.

assessment.question: When is Protocol useful?
assessment.answer: When code needs a capability rather than a shared ancestor.
assessment.explanation: It supports structural, focused interfaces for static checking, not automatic runtime enforcement.
